doc.title: Virginia Mayhew interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 23, 2022

chapter: Changes in the New York scene
title: Why fewer young people and students of color play jazz; cost of New York
summary: They discuss low diversity in school jazz, changing family listening, the internet, tuition costs, and musicians moving to Queens.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: No, but I’ve been over the years — adjudicated at many high school jazz festivals, and there’s hardly any students of color in these things. Now that could be the suburban schools but it’s not just that I don’t think. And I see it at the college level, and I suppose the sociologists have opinions on it but I’m not sure why. What is it about this music that has less appeal?

Well if you look at say even thirty years ago I was in my mid-twenties so my mom, when she was growing up — well my mom was white but that would have been the music of the time, the popular music that people of, the parents of people of my generation grew up with people still really liked jazz. You know? And the fans, the hard core fans that really knew everything, they were alive and they played the stuff for their kids and people grew up with it. But now the parents grew up in a world where it’s not really, in general, as important I think. And so then you’ve got, let’s see if there’s a parent, if there’s a 20- year-old and their parents were 20 when they had them so that would have been the 80s, late 70s that these people were born and they just don’t have the history of it being as important, especially I think the internet has had a big influence on it also. The internet. Because I don’t know it just seems like people used to, in my generation people would play records and everything is just really — family life, it just seems like with all the channels on Netflix and everything and just to sit around the house and have music it just seems like the whole society has changed and so that comes down on the parents of the kids that are going to college. Maybe — I don’t know. I don’t know who wants or doesn’t want their kid to become a jazz musician but these days, I just spoke to somebody last week who was going to the New School and he said it’s $40,000 a year.
Yes. And that is much less than many places. I mean of course the cost of living on top of that in New York City, but many of the top universities are $20,000 more than that.
How can anybody afford that? I mean other than — it’s crazy.
Yeah. And sometimes you wonder what all the jazz graduates are going to do.
Well now everybody’s moving to Queens now. Brooklyn has out-priced everybody.
So Queens is the new place.
I see. I’ll probably see an article about that in the Sunday New York Times pretty soon, in the magazine section.
About the arts moving to Queens?
